behavioral_notes.observation: On an unknown sender the partner/get and enrich_* routes call request.env['iap.enrich.api']._request_enrich({domain}) (paid IAP service) to fetch company name/address/phone/logo, then create or update a res.partner company. iap_tools._MAIL_PROVIDERS and _MAIL_DOMAIN_BLACKLIST block enriching free-mail domains (gmail.com/outlook.com). InsufficientCreditError is caught and surfaced as an enrichment_info hint. Not visible in metadata.

After IAP enrichment the controller issues an outbound requests.get(logo_url, timeout=2) to download the company logo and stores it base64 in image_1920; failures are swallowed (logged/ignored). This is a second external HTTP egress beyond the IAP RPC. Not visible in metadata.

auth='outlook' is a custom auth method: it reads the Bearer Authorization header and validates it via res.users.apikeys._check_credentials(scope='odoo.plugin.outlook'), then impersonates that user. Tokens are minted by a 2-leg flow: /auth/confirm generates an HMAC-signed auth code (3-min TTL) and /auth/access_token exchanges it for a res.users.apikeys key valid 1 day. Pure code/headers, invisible to metadata.

Logs an email into Odoo by calling message_post(body=Markup(message), attachments=...) on the target record, restricted to models in _mail_content_logging_models_whitelist() (res.partner only by default); off-whitelist models raise Forbidden. This writes a mail.message + mail.thread side-effect not declared in metadata.

IAP responses are cached in a dedicated res.partner.iap model keyed by iap_search_domain with UNIQUE(partner_id) so the same company is never enriched twice and the heavy JSON field stays off res.partner. res.partner.iap_enrich_info/iap_search_domain are compute fields mirrored from it, and res.partner.create/write transparently upsert the side-table. Relationship semantics not derivable from metadata.
2 HTTP call sites; SDKs ['requests']; api_keys=True. Outbound to IAP enrich service + third-party logo URLs; inbound auth via res.users.apikeys. This module is an outward-facing integration boundary.

No OWL/JS shipped (js_files=0): only 2 XML translation bundles (static/src/to_translate/translations_gmail.xml, translations_outlook.xml) served to the external Outlook/Gmail add-ins via /mail_plugin/get_translations. The UI lives in the third-party add-in, not in this Odoo module.

it_architecture.application: mail_plugin (Mail Plugin integration backend exposing Odoo CRM/contacts to email clients)
information_flows: inbound: Outlook/Gmail add-in -> jsonrpc routes (auth=outlook Bearer apikey)
outbound: requests.get(logo_url) -> third-party logo image fetch
side-effect: enrich_* -> res.partner company create/update + res.partner.iap cache write
external_integrations: iap.enrich.api._request_enrich -> Odoo IAP company-enrichment web service (paid, credit-metered)
res.users.apikeys (scope odoo.plugin.outlook) -> inbound Bearer-token auth for the add-ins

capabilities: Expose Contacts/CRM to Email Clients (Outlook/Gmail add-in API)
Contact Lookup & Search from the Inbox
value_streams: Email-to-CRM: open email -> resolve/enrich contact -> create partner/company -> log message back to the record
policies: Custom auth method 'outlook' gates all data routes on a scoped API key (odoo.plugin.outlook)
Free-mail / blacklisted domains excluded from IAP enrichment (_MAIL_PROVIDERS / _MAIL_DOMAIN_BLACKLIST)

classification.rationale: mail_plugin is not a primary line-of-business activity: it ships no business documents, no products, one technical model (res.partner.iap) plus two res.partner fields, and zero OWL/JS. It is an integration backend (a value-shop/network style support function, Stabell & Fjeldstad) whose job is to develop and operate an external-facing JSON API surface and token-based authorization that connects third-party systems (Outlook/Gmail add-ins) to Odoo's existing CRM/contacts data. That places it in APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' (develop/operate IT solutions and integrations), not 3.0 'Market and Sell': it re-exposes data owned by the contacts/CRM (3.0) subsystems rather than performing the selling itself, and its own assets are auth, routes and an enrichment cache. The IAP company-enrichment feature is the one business-leaning capability, but it is delivered as a technical enrichment service over the integration boundary, reinforcing the IT-enablement (support) classification.

standard_capabilities: JSON API for the official Outlook & Gmail mail plugins (partner get/search/create)
OAuth-style 2-leg authorization: HMAC auth code -> scoped res.users.apikeys access token
Custom 'outlook' auth method validating Bearer tokens
IAP-backed company enrichment (name/address/phone/logo) with domain de-duplication cache
Log email body + attachments onto a record as a mail.message
Translation feed for the add-in UI (get_translations)
typical_fits: Out-of-the-box install of the Odoo-published Outlook/Gmail add-in against this backend
Contact/company auto-creation and enrichment from the inbox using IAP credits
Single-database contact lookup scoped to the authenticated user's companies
common_gaps: Whitelisting more models for log_mail_content (override _mail_content_logging_models_whitelist) — e.g. crm.lead, helpdesk.ticket
Returning extra record context with a contact (override _get_contact_data) — done by crm/helpdesk plugin layers
Replacing IAP enrichment with a different/self-hosted data provider
Tightening token lifetime / scope policy beyond the default 1-day apikey
drive_hints: curl -X POST $ODOO/mail_plugin/auth/check_version (auth=none) -> expects 1 if module installed

open_questions: Exact IAP enrichment payload/contract (iap.enrich.api._request_enrich response shape) and credit consumption per call.
Which downstream modules extend _get_contact_data / _mail_content_logging_models_whitelist (crm, helpdesk) and what extra data they surface.
Operational token lifecycle: revocation, the 1-day apikey expiry handling, and refresh behavior in the add-ins.
